articles.title: Brydon Carse: What will it take to prevent England from more hangovers
articles.summary: Yet again, England are dealing with a player involved in a late-night incident. Only strong action will ensure there are no more, writes Stephan Shemilt.
articles.body:
Yet again, the England men's cricket team is picking through the wreckage of a late-night misdemeanour.

The latest stain on the game's reputation is a result of pictures of fast bowler Brydon Carse in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers outside a nightspot in Derby. His Durham team-mate Matthew Potts is in the images, while former England captain Ben Stokes appears in the background.

If you're keeping score, we're now up to eight England players involved in incidents of this kind since Halloween last year.

Harry Brook was punched by a nightclub bouncer in Wellington, with Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue present. Ben Duckett was filmed drunk in Noosa, then Stokes and Gus Atkinson were there when a member of England's security staff was struck in a London nightclub in June, breaching a curfew in the process.

To put it another way, there are 30 men currently on England central contracts. More than a quarter of them have been caught up in bother in the past 10 months. Of the four separate incidents, two have involved punches being thrown and another was a police matter.

In Carse's case, the time spent in handcuffs came days after new England Test captain Joe Root called on his players to be "really good role models, good human beings".

Root was speaking the day before England's first Test against Pakistan, for which Carse was part of the squad. The match was scheduled to still be ongoing when he found himself in the hands of the police.

It is understood that Carse was not arrested. Both the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and the Cricket Regulator will work to establish what happened. There are early suggestions he was denied entry back into a nightclub, or he had a drink poured over him.

Carse was also not specifically on England duty at the time. He was released from the first-Test squad to play for Durham away at Derbyshire and was scheduled to report to Lord's for the second Test on Monday.

As of Sunday evening, he remains part of the squad for the second Test. England will take time to gather some information before a decision on his involvement is made.

Root warned his squad to "be adults" when he abolished the midnight curfew - in his first act as captain - that came into place after previous incidents. As part of that move, guidelines advising players about not drinking alcohol on the day before, during or after a game, or in public, have also been removed.

There is a duty of care towards Carse. Two years ago, the 31-year-old was banned for historical betting offences and rebuilt his career to become an England regular in all three formats. No bowler has more Test wickets for England than Carse's 58 since he made his debut in October 2024.

But there is also a deep sense of anger and frustration within the ECB at having to deal with another error of judgement by a high-profile player. Supporters will take their own view, among them a sense that the behaviour of these players is now beyond parody.

Does someone have to be left out of a squad or given a meaty suspension for the penny to drop? This might be the opportunity for Root to stamp his authority on a new era.

Naturally, there will once again be the debate about not denying players their freedom or stopping them from enjoying a victory.

For Carse, a Saturday night out came less than 48 hours before he is scheduled to report for England. He is only a tweaked hamstring away from playing in a Test at Lord's on Thursday.

Perhaps more damning is the kind of trouble this group of England players seem to find. Two punch-ups and a set of handcuffs. It also does not appear to have dawned on them that they are high-profile individuals, likely to attract attention, with footage finding its way to social media, as happened with Carse.

And what about Stokes, who, despite being retired, remains an employee of the ECB via his central contract.

As the former captain, should Stokes have been conscious about Carse being in that situation? What about the trouble in which Atkinson found himself alongside Stokes in June?

Three weeks ago, Stokes denied the England team has a drinking culture, but rather that the game itself has a problem. What has Stokes done to distance himself or those around him from that drinking culture?

Now there is a wait to see what happens next. The ECB only became aware of the incident on Sunday afternoon. The governing body will take a breath overnight and decide if Carse needs to be removed from the Test squad.

Perhaps, on Tuesday, director of cricket Rob Key will once again explain why the players he manages cannot keep themselves out of trouble. In the aftermath of the Stokes-Atkinson incident in June, Key denied that England have become a "national embarrassment". He may be asked again.

Key also might be asked about the whereabouts of new Test coach Stephen Fleming, who does not take up his post until the winter. Might Carse have been less inclined to step out of line had the new sheriff been in town?

Well, here is another situation for England to manage. Only strong action will ensure there are no more.

articles.title: Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory
articles.summary: Joe Root "hacked off" by "stupid mistakes" as off-field controversy involving Brydon Carse overshadows his successful return as Test captain; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday
articles.body:
England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

articles.title: âIncredibly emotionalâ: Anaya Bangar gets Cricket Australia nod for elite womenâs cricket, eyes WBBL
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to play elite womenâs cricket in the country from March 2027.Bangar, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March, received the confirmation under Cricket Australiaâs Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision opens a pathway for her to pursue a place in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL), although she stressed that eligibility does not guarantee a franchise contract.In an exclusive conversation with Bombay Times, Anaya, daughter of former India all-rounder and batting coach Sanjay Bangar, described the development as an emotional moment after fearing that her cricket career had ended following her transition.âI am now eligible to play in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL) in Australia from March 2027 onwards. For me, this is incredibly emotional because there was a point when I genuinely believed I had lost cricket forever,â she told Bombay Times.âCricket has been such a fundamental part of my identity since childhood, and having to step away from the sport after my transition was one of the hardest things I experienced. So this isnât simply about being included in a womenâs league. It represents the possibility of returning to the sport I deeply love,â she said.Eligibility secured, but WBBL place must still be earnedAnaya was quick to clarify that Cricket Australiaâs decision only provides her with the opportunity to pursue elite womenâs cricket. She will still have to earn a place in a WBBL squad through her performances.âCricket Australia has allowed me to pursue elite womenâs cricket in Australia. The next challenge is to get myself into the best possible physical and competitive shape and put myself in a position to be considered by a WBBL franchise. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,â she said.She explained that the WBBLâs overseas-player contracting and draft system means she will have to convince a franchise of her value.âThe WBBL has an overseas-player contracting and draft system, where clubs select from the pool of available international players, like it happens in the IPL or the WPL,â Anaya said.âSo ultimately, I still have to convince a franchise that I can contribute to their team. For me, that means getting back into competitive cricket in Australian leagues, working on my batting, bowling, fielding and fitness, training consistently and demonstrating that I can perform at that level.âFrom uncertainty to a pathway in AustraliaThe development comes against the backdrop of different policies governing transgender participation in cricket.Cricket Australia has a different framework for elite domestic cricket, allowing transgender women who meet its eligibility and testosterone-related criteria to participate.Anaya said she had hoped for a clearer pathway in India but eventually chose to focus on what she could control.âWhen you grow up playing cricket competitively, the idea of potentially never being able to play again is incredibly difficult,â she said.âBut Iâve also learned that I canât build my future around waiting for somebody else to make a decision. I had to focus on what I could control â my health, my transition, my performance, the scientific evidence, and having conversations with sporting organisations.âShe added: âIâm grateful that I have a pathway in Australia, and I hope that my journey can contribute to a broader conversation about how sporting bodies can approach transgender participation with both fairness and inclusion.âCricket Australiaâs eligibility confirmation said Anayaâs determination to commence in March 2027 would not be affected by amendments to its policy. It also confirmed that she is currently eligible to participate in Premier Cricket competitions in any Australian state or territory.For Anaya, the ambition is ultimately straightforward: âI would love to reach a point where Iâm simply another cricketer competing against some of the best players in the world.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'People don't believe me': Ishan Kishan on his love for red-ball cricket
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: When Ishan Kishan walks out to bat, the image that usually comes to mind is that of a left-handed batter hitting big sixes, playing brutal .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Ishan Kishan walks out to bat, the image that usually comes to mind is that of a left-handed batter hitting big sixes, playing brutal pull shots and putting bowlers under pressure. Kishan is known for his aggressive style in white-ball cricket. But on Tuesday, the 28-year-old made it clear that he also loves the challenge of red-ball cricket.The East Zone captain led his team to a massive innings and 210-run win over North East Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru."I enjoy red-ball [cricket] very much. I think people don't believe me when I say that smiles, but it's, I'm being very honest, I really do enjoy red-ball cricket," Kishan told Cricinfo.Kishan has played 32 ODIs and 55 T20Is for India, apart from 134 IPL matches. His last of two Test appearances came in July 2023. Despite his limited opportunities in Test cricket, his love for the red-ball format remains strong."It's always fun to be part of it because I love that challenge when, you know, yes, it's easier to bat on flat tracks and it's fun as well, but the competition which goes around in Test match[es] is some different-level thing," he said.The match against North East Zone was Kishan's 65th first-class appearance. His previous first-class game was against Baroda in the Ranji Trophy in November 2025. In the nine months between the two matches, Kishan played 59 games across international and domestic cricket, including the IPL.As someone who has played plenty of white-ball cricket, he admitted that moving back to the red ball was not easy."Situations will get tricky," he said in Bengaluru, where the Duleep Trophy is being held. "It will not be easy for us as players to just move around from white ball to red ball, red ball to white ball; change of format, change of gameplay, but that is the fun part about this game," Kishan said.He spoke about the pressure and challenges that players deal with away from the field."You need to understand, as a sportsman, life can be harsh on us. It just looks very simple, like [a] player just comes here, plays their matches, and they leave. It's not like that. They go around, they keep on thinking, there's so much going on in their head every time."But Kishan believes players cannot keep making excuses if they want to succeed."If you want to make it big," Kishan said, "you want to make it count, you can't have many excuses. But at the same time, I feel you should just think about getting better and not cry about things which you cannot control."Kishan on his four-run dismissalKishan's innings in the match lasted only four runs. He reached out for a wide ball and tried to guide it behind point before being caught behind.The wicketkeeper-batter admitted that the shot came naturally and he immediately regretted playing it."I was in the middle of the shot, and I was like 'what the heck I was trying to do!' I should know this is [a] Test [first-class] match and I need to leave a few balls. So I was thinking like that, but when you don't practice so much, especially when the red ball is there [things can happen]."Kishan explained how thinking too much about not playing a shot led him to do exactly that."Sometimes when you think about something that you don't want to do, you end up doing it. I did not want to go to the ball and just play. So I ended up doing the same thing because I was thinking like I don't want to do it. I was just attracting those thoughts, which was not meant to happen, but yeah [it happened anyway]."Anukul Roy's five-for seals a big winComing back to the match, East Zone scored 467 in their first innings and then bowled North East Zone out for 111 to enforce the follow-on. North East Zone resumed Tuesday at 7 for 0. According to Kishan, East Zone's spinners were getting turn from the pitch but not much bounce. Anukul Roy picked up a five-wicket haul as North East Zone were bowled out for 146 in 50 overs. The result gave East Zone a massive innings and 210-run victory.'We'll have to be on our toes'The 2026-27 domestic red-ball season has given Kishan a fresh start, but the long break was also visible. Despite the huge victory, Kishan was not happy with East Zone's energy on the field. He wants the team to improve when they face Central Zone in the semi-final, starting on August 30."We played after a very long time, this match, but I feel the energy was not up to the mark," Kishan said, "but it can happen in these matches."When we are going to play the next match, we'll have to be on our toes. We'll have to put effort, we [will] have to fight for each and every wicket. So, we'll look into it. We'll talk, we'll have a meeting, and we'll try and put up a good show in the next game."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'A tricky one': Rahul Dravid reveals big concern over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Test future
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represen.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represented India and made his presence felt at the international level.Sooryavanshi ended the IPL 2026 season as Rajasthan Royals' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He then produced another explosive performance, smashing 94 off 29 balls against Sri Lanka 'A' in the List A tri-series final in Colombo.He made his senior India debut against England in July and followed it up with an impressive tour of Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi finished the series with 151 runs, the most by any batter, and was named Player of the Series.He has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21.However, his progress in red-ball cricket has been slower. Sooryavanshi has played eight first-class matches and averages 17.25. He is now playing for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy as he looks to gain more experience in the longer format.'I'm not sure about that'Former India head coach Rahul Dravid, who worked with Sooryavanshi at Rajasthan Royals, believes the teenager has the talent to succeed in Test cricket. But he feels there is one major hurdle - finding enough time to play domestic red-ball cricket."With Vaibhav, you've got to be patient. He's only 15 years old, and from what I've seen of the kid, I have no doubt that, given the opportunity to practice and play domestic cricket and a couple of seasons of red-ball cricket, he will be able to hold his own in a Test match team. Whether he'll be able to break into the XI with the guys already performing, that's a different story and a tricky one," Dravid told JioHotstar.Dravid's concern is not about Sooryavanshi's ability. Instead, he is worried about whether the teenager will get enough opportunities because of his growing international commitments."Whether he'll have the time to play two full seasons of domestic cricket because he'll be so busy playing for India in the white-ball format, I'm not sure about that. So skill-wise, I think there is no problem; whether he will be able to do it because of schedules might be a bit more tricky."Eight runs with the bat, two wickets with the ballSooryavanshi had a quiet outing with the bat in East Zone's Duleep Trophy quarter-final against North East Zone. The 15-year-old scored eight runs from six deliveries before Bishworjit Konthoujam dismissed him.He quickly made up for it with the ball.The East Zone vice-captain picked up two wickets in just four deliveries, showing that he could contribute even when things did not go his way with the bat.Sooryavanshi picked up his third first-class wicket with the second delivery of the 28th over. He bowled a three-quarter-length delivery outside off stump, prompting Kishan Lyngdoh to come down the track and attack. Lyngdoh tried to hit the ball hard but failed to keep his shape and produced a leading edge towards cover. Denish Das, who was fielding as a substitute, completed the catch.Three deliveries later, Sooryavanshi struck again. This time, he bowled a good-length delivery around off stump to Imliwati Lemtur. The batter tried to defend from the crease but only managed a thin outside edge. Ishan Kishan reacted quickly behind the stumps and completed the catch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: India look to wrap up Sri Lanka's innings early on Day 4 in Colombo
articles.body: India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: The tail makes India work again Sri Lanka's lower order once again proved difficult to dismiss. With Dinusha batting in a relatively open field, India concentrated on getting rid of Lahiru Kumara. But the Sri Lankan pair continued to survive. They managed to bat through more than 15 overs and showed little desire to throw their wickets away. It meant India could not get another opportunity to bowl at Sri Lanka in the fading light. The lower order had once again made India pay for not finishing the innings when they had the chance. .India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Back injury no longer a major concern for Prasidh Krishan Krishna’s rise is all the more remarkable considering the serious back injury that once threatened to derail his career. The injury required surgery and kept him out of the game for an extended period. Now 30, however, the fast bowler looks fitter, stronger and more assured. “He has learnt how to take care of his body and what it takes to have a long career. He understands his workload and follows the right strengthening programmes,” Senthilnathan said. Standing 6ft 4in, Krishna’s height remains a significant asset, allowing him to extract awkward bounce. With confidence growing, fitness concerns behind him and the backing of the team management, the Karnataka pacer increasingly looks like the strike bowler India believe he can become..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sonal Dinusha Sonal Dinusha is the third batter to have gone past 80 in each of his first three Test innings against India, after Zaheer Abbas (176, 96 and 235*) and Everton Weekes (128, 194, 162). (Weekes got hundreds in each of his first four outings vs India and was dismissed for 90 in his fifth) . A call to make - India's bowling coach Morne Morkel has not ruled out enforcing the follow-on if the opportunity presents itself, but Shubman Gill has not been particularly keen on taking that route since becoming Test captain. With the weather likely to play a part over the remaining two days, India may have to be brave with their decisions, especially with valuable WTC points up for grabs.. Time is of the essence - At 173/7, it could have all gone horribly wrong for Sri Lanka, but they have shown plenty of grit with the bat. The first task for Sonal Dinusha and Co. will be to add 39 more runs to take the follow-on out of India’s hands and, more importantly, eat up time.. Greetings, all - India dominated the first two days, but just as they did in Galle, Sri Lanka have shown that they have plenty of fight in them and will not go away quietly. There is still plenty to play for, so settle in for what promises to be another intriguing day. Reminder that play will start at 4.15 am GMT (9.45 am IST) to make up for the time lost to the weather.. ... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ....India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: India let Sri Lanka off the hook India had appeared well placed to secure a sizeable lead and potentially enforce the follow-on after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7. However, Dinusha and the lower order displayed plenty of resolve to blunt the visitors’ bowling attack. Earlier, Sri Lanka showed intent from the outset. Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis (32) stitched together an 87-run third-wicket partnership, helping the hosts add 122 runs while losing only two wickets in the opening session. Sooriyabandara brought up his maiden Test fifty off 76 balls before falling to Ravindra Jadeja while attempting a late cut. .India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sri Lanka's batters refuse to panic Despite losing wickets, Sri Lanka did not allow India to run through their batting order. The odd delivery gripped and several turned, but Sri Lanka's batters dealt with the threat posed by Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain. India also allowed the game to drift during parts of the second session, with open fields giving Sri Lanka's batters opportunities to survive. The same happened late in the day when Sonal Dinusha frustrated India alongside the lower order. .India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Dinusha leads Sri Lanka's fightback Dinusha, now the leading run-scorer of the series with 269 runs at 134.50, was closing in on a second Test century in as many matches when rain and bad light forced an early finish to the proceedings. Together with Lahiru Kumara (8 batting), he added an unbeaten 35-run stand for the ninth wicket, after earlier sharing a crucial 57-run partnership with Keshara Nuwantha (18). The 25-year-old has now registered three consecutive 80-plus scores in the series, underlining his credentials as a long-term solution to Sri Lanka’s batting woes in the middle order. With Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal unavailable, Dinusha has shouldered responsibility admirably..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Two wickets in three balls change the mood For much of the day, India had to work extremely hard for wickets. Then, suddenly, two came almost out of nowhere. Pasindu Sooriyabandara played a Ravindra Jadeja delivery back onto his own stumps. Niroshan Dickwella then edged a Mohammed Siraj delivery down the leg side to wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel. The two wickets came within three deliveries. Sri Lanka were suddenly seven down at 173. It was a huge change from the situation before lunch when they were comfortably placed at 122/3. .India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: The qualities that make Krishna dangerous One of Krishna’s biggest strengths today is his ability to combine steep bounce with a sharp leg-cutter and a well-disguised wobble-seam delivery. MRF Pace Foundation chief coach M Senthilnathan feels those qualities have helped him evolve into a bowler capable of making an impact whenever India need a breakthrough. “We always felt he had the potential to play at the highest level. Slowly, Krishna is turning into a spearhead of the Indian team and cementing his place. The most important thing is that he picks up wickets whenever he comes into the attack and breaks partnerships,” Senthilnathan said. The coach believes regular opportunities at the international level have accelerated Krishna’s growth. “The more fast bowlers play, the more confident they become. Now he feels that he belongs in the Indian team. The management has given him the confidence and they have seen that there is something special in him after all.” .India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Early exposure to Australian greats In 2016, as part of the IDBI Federal Bowling Foundation, he travelled to Australia with Tushar Deshpande and other young pacers to train under Australian fast-bowling great Jeff Thomson at Cricket Australia’s Centre of Excellence in Brisbane. Former cricket administrator Dr Makarand Waingankar believes the exposure played a significant role in Krishna’s development. “They trained under Thomson, Greg Chappell and Michael Kasprowicz. Braves could be getting a dominant bullpen weapon back just in time originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The Atlanta Braves could be getting one of their most effective relievers back before the end of the season.

Robert Suarez is expected to begin throwing bullpen sessions soon as he continues working his way back from right arm inflammation. While Atlanta has yet to establish a firm return date, Suarez's progress has kept open the possibility of a late-season return.

And based on what Suarez accomplished before going down, getting him back would be significant.

The 35-year-old has been dominant in his first season with Atlanta, posting a 4-0 record with a 0.56 ERA, four saves and 26 strikeouts across 31 appearances. Suarez has allowed just 21 hits and six walks over 32 innings, producing an impressive 0.84 WHIP.

He surrendered only two earned runs and one home run before landing on the injured list.

Braves get encouraging Robert Suarez news

Suarez hasn't pitched since June 19, when he worked 1⅓ scoreless innings against the Milwaukee Brewers . Atlanta initially described his issue as forearm soreness before placing him on the injured list with inflammation. An MRI provided encouraging news, showing no ligament damage or structural changes.

Now the focus is getting him back on a mound.

Bullpen sessions will provide Atlanta with a better indication of how close Suarez is to facing hitters. If he responds well, the next steps could include live batting practice and potentially a rehabilitation assignment before activation.

There is little reason for the Braves to rush the process.

Suarez's numbers demonstrate how valuable he can be when healthy. His ability to handle high-leverage innings provides another late-game option and could help shorten games down the stretch.

Before joining Atlanta, Suarez established himself as one of baseball's more reliable late-inning relievers with San Diego . He recorded 40 saves in 2025 and entered this season with extensive closing experience.

Atlanta doesn't necessarily need him to immediately resume a full workload.

If Suarez can return healthy and regain his command, even a limited role could strengthen the bullpen.

For now, his comeback remains a work in progress.

But after producing a 0.56 ERA through his first 31 appearances, Suarez has already shown what he can provide.

The Braves are hoping they'll get another opportunity to use it before the season ends.

articles.title: Former Australian Test cricketer  forced to retire at 27 sues school for head injury in 2014; here's why
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Australia Test batter Will Pucovski has taken legal action against Melbourne private school Brighton Grammar, alleging it failed in its duty of.
articles.body: Former Australia Test batter Will Pucovski has taken legal action against Melbourne private school Brighton Grammar, alleging it failed in its duty of care after the first concussion he suffered in 2014.According to reports in multiple Australian media outlets, Pucovski's lawyers have filed a statement of claim saying the school mishandled the head injury he suffered during an Australian rules football training session.Pucovski retired from professional cricket in April last year at the age of 27 after suffering 13 documented concussions during his career.The legal case centres on the first serious concussion he suffered as a teenager while playing football for Brighton Grammar. Pucovski was knocked unconscious during training, missed months of school after the incident, but returned to training within minutes of the hit.That injury became the first of 13 concussions he suffered before retiring from cricket on medical advice. His last match was for Victoria in 2024.Pucovski played one Test for Australia against India at the Sydney Cricket Ground in 2021. Opening the batting, he scored 62 in the first innings against an attack that included Jasprit Bumrah.He injured his shoulder while fielding during that match and missed the series-deciding Test at the Gabba. However, it was the repeated head injuries that eventually ended his cricket career.Speaking at a Lord's Taverners event earlier this year, Pucovski described how the 2014 incident changed his life."I literally got walked to the sidelines and then my only memory was the coach coming up to me and being like, 'Do you want to keep training?'. I am like, 'Yeah'. So I just went and trained for the rest of the day. It is probably the biggest day of my life in a weird way, because I have never felt the same since that day. I went from someone who would do anything and everything, to basically sitting on the couch doing nothing for an extended period," he had said, as quoted by Wisden.He developed blurred vision the following day and was admitted to hospital a week later.The International Concussion Society has warned about the risks of missed concussions in young athletes."The real concern starts when concussions are missed or inadequately addressed. This is particularly important to remember for young athletes and adolescents whose brains havenât fully matured, which makes them more susceptible to serious brain injuries."Pucovski suffered his final serious concussion in March 2024 after being hit on the head by a ball from Riley Meredith during a Sheffield Shield match. Following advice from an independent medical panel, he retired from professional cricket at the age of 27.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rafael Devers bounces a homer into McCovey Cove as Giants beat Reds 3-1
articles.summary: Rafael Devers hit his 28th homer, a drive that bounced into McCovey Cove, and reliever Anthony Molina worked 4 1/3 scoreless innings as the San Francisco Gia...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Rafael Devers hit his 28th homer, a drive that bounced into McCovey Cove, and reliever Anthony Molina worked 4 1/3 scoreless innings as the San Francisco Giants beat the Cincinnati Reds 3-1 on Tuesday night.

Drew Cavanaugh hit a two-run single in the first inning for San Francisco before Devers went deep in the fifth, his third homer in five games. It was his 16th longball at Oracle Park this season, the most by a Giant since Barry Bonds in 2007.

Sal Stewart scored the Reds' first run in 23 innings on his ninth-inning homer. His 28 home runs are the second most by a Reds rookie, trailing only Frank Robinson's 38 in 1956.

Cavanaugh finished 3 for 3 for his first career three-hit game. Nate Furman got his first major league hit, a single in the third.

Molina (1-0) relieved right-hander Adrian Houser , who left in the second inning with an apparent injury to his throwing arm. He allowed one hit and fanned a batter.

It was the second straight game in which San Francisco's starter left with an injury. Left-hander Carson Whisenhunt exited in the third inning Monday, and the team said Tuesday he has a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his pitching elbow.

Brady Singer (5-12) allowed three runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings for Cincinnati, striking out five.

articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja has spoken about the condition of Imran Khan, saying the former Pakistan Prime Minister is holding up de.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja has spoken about the condition of Imran Khan, saying the former Pakistan Prime Minister is holding up despite spending nearly three years in prison. Ramiz spoke about Imran during a recent episode of the âStick to Cricketâ podcast, where he was joined by former England captain Alastair Cook and broadcaster David Lloyd.The discussion came as concerns around Imran's health and treatment continue to grow. A group of 21 former international captains from nine cricketing nations has written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, asking for proper medical care and humane treatment for the 1992 World Cup-winning captain.Ramiz says Imran is in isolationThe conversation about Imran started after Ramiz revealed, during the podcast, that he had been convinced to take over as Pakistan Cricket Board chairman by Imran when he was Prime Minister. Lloyd then asked Ramiz about Imran's current situation.Lloyd: What are Imran Khanâs circumstances right now?Ramiz: He is in isolation. Heâs got a lot of fans, but itâs just that the poor guy has been behind bars for three years now. Itâs been a tough one for him.Cook: Is he okay, though, physically?Ramiz: Just a week back, there was some problem with his eye that seems to have been sorted, but otherwise, heâs holding up. I mean, heâs got a solid temperament, as we all know.21 former captains write to Shehbaz SharifThe comments came after 21 former international captains wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, renewing their appeal for proper medical treatment and better conditions for Imran. The group includes Indian cricket legends Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar. The appeal followed concerns that a recent medical examination did not fully meet the directions issued by Pakistan's Supreme Court.Imran, who led Pakistan to their historic 1992 World Cup triumph, has been in prison since 2023 following multiple legal cases.In their latest appeal, the former captains made three specific requests. They asked for the court-directed medical board to complete its independent assessment, for weekly family visits to continue without interruption and for any treatment recommended by the assessment to be provided without delay.Greg Chappell, who took the initiative for the letter, said: "We're not asking Pakistan for anything unusual â just that a court order most countries would take for granted is actually carried out"The signatories also made it clear that they were not seeking to interfere in Pakistan's legal proceedings."We do not presume to adjudicate Pakistanâs domestic legal processes. That is not our place, and it was not the spirit in which we wrote in February. But we do ask, again, respectfully: 1. That the medical board directed by the Supreme Court â including Mr Khanâs own doctors â be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye. 2. That the weekly family visits reinstated by the Court be honoured without interruption or administrative delay. 3. That whatever the outcome of that medical assessment, the treatment recommended by it be provided without delay. Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody. Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request. It is one we believe every nation that plays this game would recognise as fair. We hope this matter can be resolved expeditiously and with the dignity Mr Imran Khan deserves. Yours in cricket,"Among the signatories are Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Alastair Cook, Lee Germon, Adam Gilchrist, David Gower, Kim Hughes, Nasser Hussain, Clive Lloyd, Arjuna Ranatunga, Andrew Strauss, Steve Waugh and John Wright.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Gage Jump strikes out 9 and Carlos Cortes homers to lift the A's over the Twins 4-2
articles.summary: Carlos Cortes homered and Gage Jump struck out nine in 6 1/3 innings as the Athletics beat the Minnesota Twins 4-2 on Tuesday night.  Jump (6-8) pitched into...
articles.body:
WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — Carlos Cortes homered and Gage Jump struck out nine in 6 1/3 innings as the Athletics beat the Minnesota Twins 4-2 on Tuesday night.

Jump (6-8) pitched into the seventh for the first time since June 18 against the Angels , when he fanned seven and allowed one hit in seven innings.

Alika Williams got the first A's hit with a two-out double in the second, and Cortes put them ahead with a two-run shot to right field. Tommy White hit an RBI double with two outs in the sixth and Donovan Walton added a run-scoring single, extending the lead to 4-0.

Lawrence Butler had two hits for the A's, and Henry Bolte legged out his first career triple.

Taj Bradley (9-6) tied his career high with 11 strikeouts, but gave up four runs and seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. He struck out the side on nine pitches in the fifth for the first immaculate inning in Twins history .

Minnesota got two runs back in the seventh, ending Jump's night, but the Twins were held hitless the rest of the way. Hogan Harris and Luis Medina combined for 1 2/3 scoreless innings, and Elvis Alvarado earned his fourth save.

Royce Lewis led the Twins with two hits. They went 1 for 6 with runners in scoring position and stranded five overall.

LHP Connor Prielipp (3-7, 5.57 ERA) takes the mound for Minnesota opposite A's RHP J.T. Ginn (8-8, 3.60) to conclude the series on Wednesday.

articles.body: Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has criticised the International Cricket Council (ICC) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) after India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal received a light punishment for his confrontation with Sri Lanka fast bowler Asitha Fernando during the second Test in Colombo.The incident happened on the first day after Fernando dismissed Jaiswal. The two players came face to face, with Jaiswalâs helmet touching Fernandoâs forehead, before teammates stepped in to separate them.The ICC later fined both players 25 percent of their match fee and handed them one demerit point each.Manjrekar said the punishment was not enough and warned that repeated incidents could become a habit if players are not dealt with firmly.âDear ICC and BCCI, Vaibhav for India A recently & now Jaiswalâ¦ if you keep letting them get away with such behaviour, you train them to repeat such behaviour. articles.title: 'People don't believe me': Ishan Kishan on his love for red-ball cricket
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan has played 32 ODIs and 55 T20Is for India, apart from 134 IPL matches. His last of two Test appearances came in July 2023. Despite his limited o...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: When Ishan Kishan walks out to bat, the image that usually comes to mind is that of a left-handed batter hitting big sixes, playing brutal pull shots and putting bowlers under pressure. Kishan is known for his aggressive style in white-ball cricket. But on Tuesday, the 28-year-old made it clear that he also loves the challenge of red-ball cricket. The East Zone captain led his team to a massive innings and 210-run win over North East Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru. "I enjoy red-ball [cricket] very much. I think people don't believe me when I say that smiles, but it's, I'm being very honest, I really do enjoy red-ball cricket," Kishan told Cricinfo. Kishan has played 32 ODIs and 55 T20Is for India, apart from 134 IPL matches. His last of two Test appearances came in July 2023. Despite his limited opportunities in Test cricket, his love for the red-ball format remains strong. "It's always fun to be part of it because I love that challenge when, you know, yes, it's easier to bat on flat tracks and it's fun as well, but the competition which goes around in Test match[es] is some different-level thing," he said. The match against North East Zone was Kishan's 65th first-class appearance. His previous first-class game was against Baroda in the Ranji Trophy in November 2025. In the nine months between the two matches, Kishan played 59 games across international and domestic cricket, including the IPL. As someone who has played plenty of white-ball cricket, he admitted that moving back to the red ball was not easy. "Situations will get tricky," he said in Bengaluru, where the Duleep Trophy is being held. "It will not be easy for us as players to just move around from white ball to red ball, red ball to white ball; change of format, change of gameplay, but that is the fun part about this game," Kishan said. He spoke about the pressure and challenges that players deal with away from the field. "You need to understand, as a sportsman, life can be harsh on us. It just looks very simple, like [a] player just comes here, plays their matches, and they leave. It's not like that. They go around, they keep on thinking, there's so much going on in their head every time." But Kishan believes players cannot keep making excuses if they want to succeed. "If you want to make it big," Kishan said, "you want to make it count, you can't have many excuses. But at the same time, I feel you should just think about getting better and not cry about things which you cannot control."

Kishan's innings in the match lasted only four runs. He reached out for a wide ball and tried to guide it behind point before being caught behind. The wicketkeeper-batter admitted that the shot came naturally and he immediately regretted playing it. "I was in the middle of the shot, and I was like 'what the heck I was trying to do!' I should know this is [a] Test [first-class] match and I need to leave a few balls. So I was thinking like that, but when you don't practice so much, especially when the red ball is there [things can happen]." Kishan explained how thinking too much about not playing a shot led him to do exactly that. "Sometimes when you think about something that you don't want to do, you end up doing it. I did not want to go to the ball and just play. So I ended up doing the same thing because I was thinking like I don't want to do it. I was just attracting those thoughts, which was not meant to happen, but yeah [it happened anyway]."

Coming back to the match, East Zone scored 467 in their first innings and then bowled North East Zone out for 111 to enforce the follow-on. North East Zone resumed Tuesday at 7 for 0. According to Kishan, East Zone's spinners were getting turn from the pitch but not much bounce. Anukul Roy picked up a five-wicket haul as North East Zone were bowled out for 146 in 50 overs. The result gave East Zone a massive innings and 210-run victory.

The 2026-27 domestic red-ball season has given Kishan a fresh start, but the long break was also visible. Despite the huge victory, Kishan was not happy with East Zone's energy on the field. He wants the team to improve when they face Central Zone in the semi-final, starting on August 30. "We played after a very long time, this match, but I feel the energy was not up to the mark," Kishan said, "but it can happen in these matches. "When we are going to play the next match, we'll have to be on our toes. We'll have to put effort, we [will] have to fight for each and every wicket. So, we'll look into it. We'll talk, we'll have a meeting, and we'll try and put up a good show in the next game."

articles.title: 'A tricky one': Rahul Dravid reveals big concern over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Test future
articles.summary: The year 2026 has been particularly memorable for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He ended the IPL season as Rajasthan Royals' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He the...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represented India and made his presence felt at the international level. Sooryavanshi ended the IPL 2026 season as Rajasthan Royals' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He then produced another explosive performance, smashing 94 off 29 balls against Sri Lanka 'A' in the List A tri-series final in Colombo. He made his senior India debut against England in July and followed it up with an impressive tour of Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi finished the series with 151 runs, the most by any batter, and was named Player of the Series. He has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21. However, his progress in red-ball cricket has been slower. Sooryavanshi has played eight first-class matches and averages 17.25. He is now playing for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy as he looks to gain more experience in the longer format.

Former India head coach Rahul Dravid, who worked with Sooryavanshi at Rajasthan Royals, believes the teenager has the talent to succeed in Test cricket. But he feels there is one major hurdle - finding enough time to play domestic red-ball cricket. "With Vaibhav, you've got to be patient. He's only 15 years old, and from what I've seen of the kid, I have no doubt that, given the opportunity to practice and play domestic cricket and a couple of seasons of red-ball cricket, he will be able to hold his own in a Test match team. Whether he'll be able to break into the XI with the guys already performing, that's a different story and a tricky one," Dravid told JioHotstar. Dravid's concern is not about Sooryavanshi's ability. Instead, he is worried about whether the teenager will get enough opportunities because of his growing international commitments. "Whether he'll have the time to play two full seasons of domestic cricket because he'll be so busy playing for India in the white-ball format, I'm not sure about that. So skill-wise, I think there is no problem; whether he will be able to do it because of schedules might be a bit more tricky."

Eight runs with the bat, two wickets with the ball

Sooryavanshi had a quiet outing with the bat in East Zone's Duleep Trophy quarter-final against North East Zone. The 15-year-old scored eight runs from six deliveries before Bishworjit Konthoujam dismissed him. He quickly made up for it with the ball. The East Zone vice-captain picked up two wickets in just four deliveries, showing that he could contribute even when things did not go his way with the bat. Sooryavanshi picked up his third first-class wicket with the second delivery of the 28th over. He bowled a three-quarter-length delivery outside off stump, prompting Kishan Lyngdoh to come down the track and attack. Lyngdoh tried to hit the ball hard but failed to keep his shape and produced a leading edge towards cover. Denish Das, who was fielding as a substitute, completed the catch. Three deliveries later, Sooryavanshi struck again. This time, he bowled a good-length delivery around off stump to Imliwati Lemtur. The batter tried to defend from the crease but only managed a thin outside edge. Ishan Kishan reacted quickly behind the stumps and completed the catch.

articles.title: IND vs SL 2nd Test: Sri Lanka's last three pairs produce rare resistance against India, survive 40-plus overs

articles.body: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha continued his impressive form with the bat, scoring his second century in as many Tests against India. However, the 25-year-old's effort was not enough to prevent India from enforcing the follow-on in the second Test on Wednesday.Sri Lanka were bowled out for 290 after India had declared their first innings at 503/9. That gave India a 213-run lead and allowed them to send Sri Lanka back to bat immediately.India lead the two-Test series 1-0 after their 165-run win in Galle.Sri Lanka's lower order keeps India waitingSri Lanka's last three pairs showed plenty of fight after the team was reduced to 265/8. They stayed at the crease for more than 40 overs before the innings finally ended.It was only the second time Sri Lanka's last three pairs, from the eighth to the 10th wicket, had survived for more than 40 overs against India in a Test innings.The earlier instance came at the P Sara Oval in 2010. Sri Lanka were 87/7 in 31.2 overs but managed to reach 267 before being bowled out in 85.2 overs. Their last three pairs batted for 54 overs.The most recent such instance against India came in Pune in 2019, when South Africa's last three pairs survived for 61.2 overs. South Africa were 139/7 in 44.2 overs before being dismissed for 275.Dinusha completes another centuryDinusha resumed the day unbeaten on 85 and immediately looked to score quickly.He attacked debutant off-spinner Saransh Jain in the first over, hitting him for a six and a four to move into the nineties. In the following over, he completed his second successive Test century with a boundary off Prasidh Krishna.Dinusha eventually fell for 103 off 162 balls, with eight fours and three sixes.He had also scored a century and an 84 in the first Test in Galle, making him Sri Lanka's standout batter across the two matches so far.Saransh makes his markSaransh gave India their first breakthrough of the day when he dismissed Lahiru Kumara to claim his maiden Test wicket.The debutant later removed Dinusha to end the left-hander's resistance. He finished with 1/45.Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar were India's leading wicket-takers, claiming three wickets each. Prasidh finished with 3/52 and Suthar with 3/85.Sri Lanka's lower order made India work hard for the final wickets, but the 213-run deficit meant the hosts had no way to escape the follow-on.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ETPL: Who are the Belfast Wolves and Dublin Guardians in new European T20 league?
articles.summary: The Belfast Wolves and Dublin Guardians will play their first game of the European T20 Premier League in Voorburg on Thursday.
articles.body:
After much talk and a few false dawns, a European franchise league will finally get under way this week.

The European T20 Premier League (ETPL) will be run in collaboration with the cricket boards of Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands with big names such as Rahul Dravid and Steve Waugh all involved in off-field roles.

There will be a number of high-profile players in action too.

Of the six teams, one will be based in Dublin and one, notionally, in Belfast - more on that later - with the pair playing each other in their first game on Thursday.

Waugh invests in European T20 Premier League Published 20 January

Waugh invests in European T20 Premier League

ETPL a 'wonderful opportunity' to grow cricket Published 17 August

ETPL a 'wonderful opportunity' to grow cricket

Dravid named as Dublin franchise co-owner for ETPL Published 11 May

Dravid named as Dublin franchise co-owner for ETPL

Both the Wolves and Guardians will feature a mix of familiar names from the local and international scene.

The Wolves, who have adopted a motto of "family, fearless, and fun", will be captained by experienced Australian all-rounder Glenn Maxwell.

IPL veteran David Miller, who has a 35-ball T20 century to his name, and New Zealand wicketkeeper Devon Conway will be relied upon to provide spark in the order.

The bowling attack, meanwhile, will boast the talents of Chris Jordan whose various claims to fame include being a World Cup winner, taking more T20 wickets for England than anyone not named Adil Rashid, and being a former school-mate of Rihanna.

There will be a strong local presence too with Mark Adair, Matthew Humphreys and Ireland's one-day captain Paul Stirling among their number.

That trio will be joined by international team-mates Gavin Hoey, Tim Tector and Lorcan Tucker, some of whom no doubt may find it a touch strange to be playing against a team representing Dublin.

The Guardians own Irish contingent will be provided by Craig Young, Matthew Hollard, Josh Little, George Dockrell, Benjamin Calitz and Harry Tector.

They will be supplemented by New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell who, fresh from his unbeaten Test century against England at Trent Bridge in June, will be one of the league's star attractions, while former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin was announced as captain and mentor of the side in July.

The competition will run from 26 August to 20 September in a double-round robin format. The first half of the pool stage will be staged in the Netherlands with the second round of games taking place in Dublin.

That means that the Belfast franchise, along with those in Glasgow and Edinburgh, will not play at home in the first year of the competition.

Already, however, there have been talks about potentially staging games at Stormont in future seasons.

The first Belfast versus Dublin derby will be played in Voorburg on Thursday with the "reverse" fixture taking place at Malahide in Dublin on 9 September.

What about the other Ireland players involved?

The Irish internationals will be spread further afield than just the Belfast and Dublin franchises.

Jordan Neill and Curtis Campher will be team-mates of Steve Smith, Mitchell Marsh and Tim David with Amsterdam, while Jai Moondra parlayed his recent international exposure into a first-round draft selection by Rotterdam Dockers where he will team up with Faf Du Plessis.

Gareth Delany and Ross Adair will represent the Edinburgh Castle Rockers, with the latter set to first go head-to-head with his brother Mark on 2 September.

articles.summary: Cricket News: New Gulf Giants head coach Simon Helmot believes smart recruitment and a fearless identity are the keys to returning the inaugural ILT20 champions to .
articles.body: New Gulf Giants head coach Simon Helmot believes smart recruitment and a fearless identity are the keys to returning the inaugural ILT20 champions to title contention. In a conversation with TimesofIndia.com, the Australian coach discussed marquee signings of Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Azmatullah Omarzai, Blessing Muzarabani, their auction strategy, squad balance, and the culture he wants to build at the ILT20 franchise.Excerpts:Q. You're in the Caribbean right now. Talk about where you are and what took you there.Simon Helmot: I've been involved with the CPL (Caribbean Premier League) for seven years now. Originally I began in Trinidad before KKR (Knight Riders Group) took over. And then the last four seasons I've been involved with the St. Kitts and Nevis Patriots. Had some success with Trinidad (Trinbago Knight Riders) in 2015 and had some success with the Patriots in 2021. So hoping to have some success with the Gulf Giants in 2026.Q. When did the Gulf Giants association come about? How did that process unfold?Helmot: I've been involved with the Desert Vipers in the ILT20 for the first four editions of the competition. An opportunity came about, I spoke to the Gulf Giants after last season. To take on the role as a head coach was certainly an honour and one that I'm really looking forward to getting stuck into.Q. Gulf Giants have signed David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen before the auction. What gaps were you looking to address?Helmot: Compiling any T20 squad, you need to try and have a balanced team. And probably an area we felt we hadn't done so well was that middle to back end. So making sure we can shore up that middle-order strength was important for us with the pre-signings.I suppose you always try and get the best talent you possibly can, and then you might need to move the deck chairs around come auction time with the areas you still need to balance and shape your squad.I've worked with Klaasen with Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL. David Miller has been in the opposition camp most of the time in the competitions I've been involved with. They're both proven cricketers, proven leaders, and I'm really looking forward to working with them.The timing also works perfectly now that the ILT20 and SA20 don't clash. They'll be available for the whole tournament before heading home for Christmas and then into the SA20.Q. How do you see Miller, Klaasen and Azmatullah Omarzai fitting into the batting order?Helmot: There's also Azmat â another pre-signing and one of the best players to come from Afghanistan. With those three players, that No. 4-6 area can be arranged in any way.T20 cricket these days is about entrance points, preferred match-ups and game situations. There's an element of flexibility with those three players, and it also depends on who we secure at the auction.We'll still need some top-order players, continue strengthening our spin component, and add pace depth. There are a few more pieces to the puzzle, but those four signings â Klaasen, Miller, Azmat and Blessing Muzarabani â give us an excellent foundation.Q. Omarzai and Muzarabani were key retentions. What made them so important?Helmot: It's all about skillsets, and Azmat is such a versatile player. He can bowl in any stage of an innings and bat in the middle order or in the finishing role. He's an intelligent cricketer who's played some outstanding cricket over the last couple of seasons. Keeping him, especially with the new rule allowing four Afghan players in a squad, was a no-brainer.Blessing unfortunately was injured last year, so he couldn't feature. But he's been involved with the Gulf Giants before and he's a very good frontline fast bowler. Now it's about adding the right players around them to create a versatile attack with both pace and spin, while also strengthening the top order.Q. What does your auction strategy look like, especially with the ILT20's unique squad rules?Helmot: It's a fascinating challenge, and I'm sure every team is asking the same question. The regulations around UAE players, Afghan players, Associates, Gulf-region players and the Irish player requirement all play a major role.Ultimately, auctions are about acquiring talent, experience and players who complement each other. We'll also have a wildcard available during the process. So we're looking for players in form, players we can secure at the right price, and players who help us build a balanced squad within the salary cap.The different venues also matter enormously. Sharjah, Abu Dhabi and Dubai can all play differently â sometimes pace-friendly, sometimes spin-friendly. Our squad has to be versatile enough to adapt, while also ensuring we have quality replacements for injuries, form or venue-specific selections.Q. Is there an ideal squad size for a tournament like the ILT20?Helmot: I think it depends on the tournament length and the regulations. I've always liked slightly smaller squads in the IPL because you can concentrate more on the players who are genuinely in contention to play.For the ILT20, I think 20 players is a really good number. If you have 21 or 22, that's fine too. There's no exact science â you simply need enough cover for injuries and emergencies without stretching your coaching resources across too many players who may never get on the field.Q. With such a short tournament, how do you build team chemistry quickly?Helmot: There are two parts to it. The first is communication before the season even starts. Once the auction is done, we've got around six weeks to speak with players, understand their calendars and begin building relationships.Some players, especially the UAE players, will arrive early, and that's a great opportunity to make them feel valued and connected to the Giants family. As everyone else arrives, it's about creating strong team dynamics through training, practice games and informal interactions.After 20 years in franchise cricket, I'm very comfortable bringing together players from different countries. It requires organisation, off-field planning and really good people. Thankfully, we've got excellent assistant coaches, medical staff and supportive ownership to help create that environment.Q. Finally, what will be the identity of Simon Helmot's Gulf Giants?Helmot: We're going to play a bold, exciting brand of cricket. We'll assess conditions smartly, but we'll play aggressive, tough cricket. Any team that comes up against us should know they're in for a hell of a fight.I want us to do that with confidence, calmness and a smile on our face â both on the field and in the dugout.I've been fortunate to be part of the ILT20 since it began, so I understand the environment well. It's a wonderful tournament because the travel is so manageable, and that helps create a close-knit franchise culture. Good teams connect quickly, whether that's through structured social activities or simply having a great team room where players and families enjoy spending time together.The Gulf Giants were the first champions of this competition. Our priority is to get back into the playoffs and finals, and then go as deep into the tournament as possible.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Very rarely do I get the chance to play red-ball cricket': Arshdeep Singh after North Zoneâs 52-run win in Duleep Trophy
articles.summary: Cricket News: India pacer Arshdeep Singh is hoping his return to first-class cricket can strengthen his case for a Test debut. The 27-year-old, who has played 18 OD.
articles.body: India pacer Arshdeep Singh is hoping his return to first-class cricket can strengthen his case for a Test debut. The 27-year-old, who has played 18 ODIs and 91 T20Is, had not played a red-ball game for nearly a year before featuring in the 2026 Duleep Trophy.Arshdeep played a key role in North Zoneâs 52-run win over West Zone in Bengaluru, taking 3/53 and 1/40 across the two innings.âVery rarely do I get the chance to play red-ball cricket, and this was a chance. I wanted to showcase my skill set and just see how many overs I can bowl. The rhythm feels nice. After a long time, I was playing a red-ball game. I put in a lot of hours in practice, and it felt nice. The body is sore, but itâs a good sore because we got the win,â Arshdeep said after the game, as quoted by Cricinfo.Arshdeep said he changed his training routine before the Duleep Trophy, focusing specifically on bowling with the red ball.âThis time around, I knew the Duleep Trophy was coming, I was practising with red ball. When white-ball season is coming, then you practice with the white ball. Itâs very specific training based on what kind of season is coming in front of you,â he added.He said red-ball cricket gives bowlers repeated chances to trouble batters.âAjay Sharma, our head coach, just told me that âeven if you donât get wickets with the new ball, you have a chance to come back in the second spellâ. Red ball has that beauty of giving you a chance again,â he said.Experience and adaptabilityArshdeep, who played five County Championship matches for Kent in 2023, said county cricket remains valuable but Indiaâs packed schedule makes another stint difficult.âWhenever you get a chance, whenever there is a time frame you can go to England to play county cricket, that is a really good experience, but now, with the IPL, the white-ball season at home, and domestic cricket also going on, you canât go play county. There are crucial games getting played here. We want to push our domestic cricket as well and make sure the level doesnât drop down. We all choose to play here and give our best,â he said.On Bengaluruâs pitch, Arshdeep said bowlers had to rely more on tactics than movement.âOn wickets like this, you just have to play with the mind. Sometimes you get success, sometimes you get hit for across-the-line six as well. So you got to take both and just keep trying,â he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brydon Carse: Josh Tongue says Joe Root's message to England players has "100%" landed
articles.summary: Fast bowler Josh Tongue said captain Joe Rootâs message to the England players about their off-field behaviour has â100%â been heeded.
articles.body:
Fast bowler Josh Tongue said captain Joe Root's message to the England players about their off-field behaviour has "100%" been heeded.

On Tuesday, Root said he was "hacked off" that Brydon Carse had become the latest England player involved in a late-night drinking controversy.

The skipper also revealed he had addressed the squad before they began training in preparation for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's, beginning on Thursday.

"It was a chat that was needed, a very good chat from Rooty," Tongue told BBC Sport.

"He was very clear on the message of what it is like to be an England cricketer. We're very privileged to put on that England shirt and we want to show kids growing up how good it is to play for England in front of thousands of people."

Carse has been removed from the England squad for the second Test after he was briefly arrested while on a night out in Derby on Saturday.

Footage of the 31-year-old in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers appeared on social media on Sunday.

He was eventually de-arrested, but the England and Wales Cricket Board have referred the matter to the Cricket Regulator, and the Regulator's investigation has resulted in Carse's absence from the squad for Lord's.

It is the latest in a string of controversies involving the England men's team over the past 10 months.

Only last week, before the first Test in his second spell as captain, Root called on his players to be "really good role models and good human beings".

This week, Root made no attempt to hide his frustration at "stupid mistakes".

On what Root said to the players, Tongue revealed: "He was honest with us all in the changing room. He said it straight. As soon as that chat was finished, our focus was fully on these next five days."

Asked if the message had "landed", Nottinghamshire's Tongue replied: "Yeah, 100%. What has happened in the past is the past and we need to try to move on from that."

Root 'hacked off' and 'disappointed' at Carse incident

Punishment to send a shiver needed - Vaughan

Tongue is one of the eight England centrally contracted players to have been involved in or present for a late-night drinking incident since last October.

The 28-year-old was with Harry Brook when the England white-ball captain was punched by a nightclub bouncer in Wellington.

The Regulator took no action against Tongue for his part in the controversy, but the paceman admitted he was forced to reflect on his involvement and the fragility of a career as an England cricketer.

"I want to play for England for as long as I can," he said. "I've tried to forget about that as much as I can and focus on the cricket here, now."

Tongue was part of a four-pronged pace attack that led England to an innings victory over Pakistan in the first Test at Headingley.

Victory over the tourists at Lord's would give England their first win in a multi-match series since 2024.

The hosts seem likely to name an unchanged XI, the first time they have gone unchanged between matches since the first and second Tests at home to India last summer.

England are currently under interim head coach Marcus Trescothick, with New Zealander Stephen Fleming due to take charge from the tour of South Africa in December.

In Leeds, Root confirmed he had been in daily contact with Fleming, and Tongue has also heard from the incoming coach.

"He messaged me the day before the Test, touching on The Hundred and congratulating me on that, and saying good luck for the first Test," said Tongue.

"Then he messaged me after the first day as well, which was very nice. Obviously, he wants to have a look at everyone before coming in for the South Africa series. It's nice to know that he's been watching."

articles.title: England captain Joe Root urges side to 'earn back trust' of nation following Brydon Carse incident ahead of second Pakistan Test
articles.summary: England return to action on Thursday following another off-field controversy; a video emerged over the weekend of England bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed by police outside a nightclub; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday
articles.body:
Root was reinstalled to the role ahead of the series after Ben Stokes' retirement from international cricket, which followed the former captain being involved in an off-field controversy during this summer's series defeat to New Zealand.

After Root enjoyed the perfect return to captaincy with a dominant victory at Headingley, video footage emerged of fast bowler Brydon Carse, who had been part of the England squad for the first Test before being released to play for his county, being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen in the video talking to Durham team-mate Matthew Potts, with Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Test at Lord's, which begins on Thursday, with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator under way.

After admitting he was "hacked off" at the latest controversy, Root attempted to put a positive spin on the situation by pointing to the opportunity he and incoming Test head coach Stephen Fleming have to alter the public's perception of their side.

Speaking on Tuesday, Root said: "Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen, and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Tongue: Root has made clear what he expects from us

England fast bowler Josh Tongue, who is expected to keep his place in what is likely to be an unchanged XI at Lord's, said Root has reiterated his expectations of the squad.

Tongue said on Wednesday: "We had a chat before training yesterday as Joe said. It was a very good conversation and he made it clear what he expects from us.

"He's been around the England dressing room for plenty of years now, he knows what it takes to be the top professional and we've just got to do the best we can moving forward.

"We've just got to make sure we're as professional as we can be. Obviously things have happened and we need to try and move on from them to show all the youngsters growing up wanting to play for England that it's an amazing place to be.

"Playing for England is obviously a privilege. We want to give the next generation the best place that they can be really."

The only change to England's squad for the game is Carse being replaced by 23-year-old quick Sonny Baker, who made his Test debut against New Zealand in June.

articles.body: Sri Lanka showed some fight on day four of the second Test, but Indiaâs bowlers struck at crucial moments to leave the hosts at 229 for six in their second innings.Rain and bad light stopped play before India could finish the job, leaving Sri Lanka needing another strong effort to avoid a series defeat.Sri Lanka had earlier been forced to follow on after being bowled out for 290, falling 13 runs short of the follow-on mark. Sonal Dinusha was the standout performer, scoring 103 for his second century of the series.Sooriyabandara and Mendis lead the fightbackSri Lanka lost their openers early in the second innings, but Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis changed the momentum with a 115-run partnership. The pair attacked the Indian bowlers and helped Sri Lanka recover from 63 for two.Mendis hit Manav Suthar for two sixes and reached his half-century with another six, while Sooriyabandara soon followed with a 78-ball fifty.Prasidh Krishna eventually broke the partnership, with Shubman Gill taking a running catch to dismiss Mendis for 55. Sri Lanka reached tea at 199 for three, just 14 runs away from avoiding an innings defeat.India strike lateThe final session belonged to India as they picked up three more wickets. Dhananjaya de Silva was dismissed by Suthar before Sooriyabandara, who was closing in on his maiden Test century, threw away his wicket while charging at the spinner. Rishabh Pant completed the stumping.Saransh Jain then dismissed Niroshan Dickwella to reduce Sri Lanka to 218 for six. India had nearly an hour to finish the innings, but heavy rain ended play at 4:37 pm.Earlier, Dinusha completed his century with a powerful pull off Prasidh.
