articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka: A hold, the choke and then the frustrating close
articles.summary: Cricket News: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: Sonal Dinusha, dark clouds, rain and the close of play. There has been no deviation in the last three days, but Day 4 of .
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: Sonal Dinusha, dark clouds, rain and the close of play. There has been no deviation in the last three days, but Day 4 of the Test saw a finish earlier than what we saw in the previous two days. After a hard-fought day of Test cricket, both teams were off the field as relentless rain forced an early close. The equation: India need four wickets to close Sri Lanka's innings and then chase it down to complete the clean sweep.The beauty of a day of Test cricket is its ability to dish out moments and periods that can swing the momentum either way, yet keep both parties interested. Day 4 followed that pattern and saw India toil hard, Sri Lanka put up a proper fight and then witnessed the visitors claw their way back with three quick wickets in the final session.India went through the motions in the first two sessions, failing to be as "brave" as bowling coach Morne Morkel had expected after enforcing the follow-on. They not only lacked innovation but were also unable to control the proceedings, allowing easy runs to the Lankan batters. The fields the spinners were bowling to, and the consistent protection offered for the reverse sweep, were baffling and spoke to a defensive mindset. As many as four fielders remained on the ropes, while those in the ring were positioned deep enough to be away from the batter's uncomfortable eyeline."I think that was what the discussion was all about between Gautam, the captain and all the spinners. We wanted to hold that position and that is why we had open fields," spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule told the media after the end of day's play."The spinners were assigned different roles and they all played their part to perfection. The beauty of Test cricket is such that things can quickly change in sessions, so that is what we saw, where we picked wickets in the final session," he explained further.The ordinary bowling didn't help, as Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain collectively lacked control and a plan for the fluent approach taken by Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis. The left-right pair was very busy, feasted on some ordinary bowling and kept the board ticking with open fields that offered comfortable singles.Pasindu, in particular, operated with a sense of fluent urgency, and neither he nor Mendis allowed Suthar to settle into a rhythm. Suthar, India's most impressive bowler from the first Test, leaked runs at over six an over off his first eight overs, which definitely played a part in captain Shubman Gill resorting to defensive fields."As I said, that was the plan. With regards to Manav Suthar, he is a quality bowler and experiences like these will only help him adapt and understand his game better," said Bahutule.The fast bowlers also showed one-dimensional planning, as the short ball remained their only ploy. Prasidh Krishna operated with men in catching positions for mistimed hooks and pulls. While he did manage to pick up a wicket with the trap, the period lacked creativity and the bravado that was needed at the hour. India never looked like constructing a proper spell with sustained pressure from both ends. The only out-of-the-box thought came against Pasindu when Rishabh Pant moved up to the stumps to restrict the batter to the crease.Two men in catching positions on the leg side seemed a well-thought-out plan, and it planted seeds of doubt in the right-hander, who was playing only his third Test innings. The movement was restricted, fluency was halted, and Suthar capitalised on the batter's itchiness when he pushed one way outside the off stump, catching the batter out of his crease. Pant completed the formalities and India collectively sighed in relief after dismissing the batter who had made them toil hard in both innings.It was Suthar's second wicket in as many overs, and when Saransh Jain got Niroshan Dickwella early, it was up to the bowlers to wrap up the lower order in a hurry. Had the heavy rain not arrived early, Sri Lanka would have been in for a tough time because there was a rare period of 36 deliveries when not a single run was scored. After the hold, India managed to apply the choke, even if only briefly, setting up an exciting Day 5. For India, enforcing the follow-on was a no-brainer, and the entire group reached a collective agreement without debate."We have been keeping an eye on the clouds since rain has been around from Galle. So we were ready to enforce the follow-on and so were the bowlers. To have the best shot," said Bahutule.The clouds will continue to attract the attention they have had in the last few weeks, and India would hope the dark, grey formations remain away from the stadium, allowing them to bundle out Sri Lanka early and then chase whatever target is set for them. In Bahutule's words, there is a familiar "thorn in the flesh", Sonal, standing between them and 2-0.Brief ScoresIndia: 503 for 9 declaredSri Lanka: 290 & 229 for 6 (Pasindu Sooriyabandara 92, Kamindu Mendis 50; Manav Suthar 2/81, Prasidh Krishna 1/31)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: âAbsolute shameâ: DDCA draws flak over DPL player-selection rule amid Dev Chaudhary row
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The inclusion of little-known cricketer Dev Chaudhary by New Delhi Tigers has raised serious questions over the Delhi Premier Leagueâs play.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The inclusion of little-known cricketer Dev Chaudhary by New Delhi Tigers has raised serious questions over the Delhi Premier Leagueâs player-selection rules and put the Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA) under scrutiny.New Delhi Tigers are currently last among the eight teams, with just one win from 10 matches. Chaudhary played two games as an opener, scoring 0 off 2 balls against South Delhi Superstarz and 16 off 24 against West Delhi Lions.His second innings, in particular, drew attention because of his unusual batting stance and inability to hit a single powerful shot. He also played five dot balls to a spinner during the Powerplay, leaving players, coaches and officials questioning how he made the playing XI.Rule under scrutinyThis season, the DPL allowed each franchise to select three players outside the auction, with the only requirement being that they had played at least five DDCA League matches.Several DDCA Apex Council members had opposed the rule, fearing it could allow undeserving players to enter the league through recommendations. Lawyer and Apex Council member Shyam Sharma said he had raised concerns about it before the rule was approved."It has been an absolute shame. I was the first one who had raised my voice about this rule. They made a criteria that five DDCA League games would be enough to qualify for a place in DPL without auction."Now I had asked on the forum, what if that guy hasn't performed and picked. Dev Chaudhary has been exposed but there are many players like this who have come into the teams on recommendations," Sharma told PTI.Sharma said he has again asked the Apex Council to reconsider the rule and make the necessary changes. DDCA secretary Ashok Sharma confirmed the rule would be examined."The Rule will be reviewed once the tournament is over," he added.Questions over Chaudhary's selectionLittle is known about Chaudhary's cricketing background, apart from his participation in Delhi U-19 trials. He played DDCA League matches for Sporting Club, which has also been associated with India pacer Prince Yadav.A club source claimed Chaudhary was recommended by former India U-19 and Delhi pacer Pradeep Sangwan and played only two matches before the club advised his father not to send him back."He was recommended by former India U19 and Delhi pacer Pradeep Sangwan. He played two games and after that one of our senior club official called his father and told him that 'Please don't send your son as he isn't good enough'." The source added that the club was stunned to later see him playing in the DPL.New Delhi Tigers are coached by Dronacharya Award winner and Virat Kohli's childhood coach Rajkumar Sharma. Neither Sharma nor team owner Ajay Kumar responded to PTI's calls and messages seeking clarification on Chaudhary's selection.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
The premier qualification tournament for Associate cricket teams in Asia gets underway with the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 in Malaysia, running from August 30 to September 12.

Organized by the Asian Cricket Council, sponsored and live streamed by Dafanews, the tournament sees 10 of Asia's leading associate nations chasing not just the title but a direct route into the 2027 Men's Asia Cup .

Hosted across two venues near Kuala Lumpur, it follows a group stage and knockout structure with the format switching back to 50-over cricket this year after the previous edition in Oman was played as a T20I event.

ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026: Live stream, TV Channel

Live Streaming: Match details and updates of the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 will be on Dafanews.

How to watch: Getting started only takes a couple of minutes. Create a Dafabet account, navigate to the live sports tab, and every fixture becomes available to follow, complete with ball-by-ball scores and updates as they happen.

When is the ACC Men's Premier Cup? Dates and full schedule

Tournament Duration: The ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 runs from August 30 to September 12, with a short gap built in before the knockout matches.

Match Format: The group stage plays out with two matches most days, one at each venue, before the tournament narrows to the semifinals.

Daily Timings: All group games are scheduled for a 9:30 AM start in Malaysian Standard Time.

League Stage: The group phase wraps up on September 8, after which the top two sides from each group advance.

Knockout Stage: Both semifinals take place on September 10, followed by a rest day before the tournament concludes.

Third-Place Playoff and Final: The third-place playoff and the grand final are both held on September 12, closing out the tournament.

Teams in Action: Nepal, Hong Kong China, Malaysia, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia , United Arab Emirates, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar and Singapore.

Tournament Structure: The 10 teams are split into two groups of five, Group A and Group B, with every side playing the other four teams in its group once.

Qualification Rules: The top two teams from each group qualify for the semifinals, with the group winners and runners-up crossing over (A1 faces B2, and B1 faces A2) before the final decides the champion.

Match Rules: Games are played under 50-over ODI regulations, a change from the T20I format used at the 2024 edition in Oman.

Team Composition: The field brings together some of Asia's most established associate sides, including defending champions United Arab Emirates and 2023 winners Nepal, alongside Oman, who reached the final in 2024.

articles.title: 'Give supporters reasons to stay': Ramiz Raja warns Pakistan cricket amid poor results in Tests
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s struggles are beginning to show beyond the scorecard, with former captain Ramiz Raja warning that the team’s poor performances are costing .
articles.body: Pakistan’s struggles are beginning to show beyond the scorecard, with former captain Ramiz Raja warning that the team’s poor performances are costing them something even more valuable, the support of their fans.Pakistan were thrashed by England by an innings and 103 runs in the opening Test at Headingley, with their batting collapsing for 171 and 135. England’s bowlers, led by Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue, claimed eight wickets apiece as the hosts wrapped up the contest inside three days.‘They’ve already lost a lot of fans’Speaking on a cricket podcast with former England captains Alastair Cook and Michael Vaughan, Ramiz said Pakistan’s repeated setbacks were contributing to a growing disconnect with supporters.“Social media is after them. They’ve already lost a lot of fans. So it’s become a norm when you lose a Test match, it’s become another loss and it means another lot of fans withdrawing from cricket,” Ramiz said.The former Pakistan skipper, who also served as PCB chairman, stressed that rebuilding and retaining the fan base should be a priority.“I think Pakistan needs to give supporters reasons to stay behind them. I have always believed that when you start losing fans and supporters, the first pillar probably has fallen. To become a great side you need to have fans behind you and it is vice-versa,” he added.Pakistan now have little time to regroup. The second Test begins at Lord’s on Thursday, with England holding a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.Babar return offers Pakistan hopeThe biggest positive heading into the second Test is the likely return of Babar Azam. The Pakistan captain missed the Headingley opener with a finger injury, but he has resumed full batting practice and faced both fast bowlers and spinners in the nets at Lord’s.For England, the challenge will be to maintain the intensity that produced such a dominant opening performance. Joe Root began his second stint as Test captain with an emphatic win, while the pace attack exposed Pakistan’s vulnerability against quality seam bowling.The Lord’s Test, starting on August 27, therefore presents Pakistan with an immediate chance to respond. A victory would level the series and restore some belief; another defeat would give England an unassailable 2-0 lead ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston from September 9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dean Elgar announces retirement from professional cricket after 20-year career
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former South Africa Test captain Dean Elgar has announced that he will retire from all professional cricket at the end of the 2026 County C.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former South Africa Test captain Dean Elgar has announced that he will retire from all professional cricket at the end of the 2026 County Championship season, bringing the curtain down on a career spanning more than two decades.The 39-year-old left-handed opener confirmed his decision through Essex, where he has continued to make a significant impact in county cricket after calling time on his international career in January 2024. Elgar said the decision was largely driven by a desire to spend more time with his family in South Africa.“I feel it's the right time for me now. I'm not getting any younger, 39 years old, and I've got a lot of things going on back home with regards to a young but growing-up-very-quickly family. It's the right time for me now to be present at home and be there for my partner and my kids,” Elgar said, as quoted by Essex Cricket.“It’s been a great journey so far. It’s not done yet, but at the end of the season, I will be retiring,” he added.A career built on resilienceElgar leaves the game as one of South Africa's most dependable Test openers. He played 86 Tests, scoring 5,347 runs at an average of 37.92, with 14 centuries and a highest score of 199. Across first-class cricket, he amassed 18,981 runs in 279 matches at an average of 41.90, underlining the longevity and consistency that defined his career.He also captained South Africa in 18 Tests, with his tenure producing one of his most cherished memories, a memorable victory over England at Lord's.“Beating England at Lord's as captain is one of them. That stands out quite profoundly, purely the way we played cricket and the style and brand in which we played it,” Elgar said.A specialist in tough conditionsElgar built his reputation on an old-fashioned quality: the ability to bat for long periods and absorb pressure. He carried his bat through an entire Test innings three times during his international career and became the only batter to achieve the feat twice in the same calendar year, doing so in 2018.His international career ended after South Africa's Test series against India in January 2024, but Elgar continued to play professionally with Essex.Following in Cook's footsteps at EssexJoining Essex came with its own challenge. Elgar inherited the opening role previously occupied by England great Alastair Cook, but he quickly established himself in his own way. He scored more than 1,000 runs in his first season with the county and was named Essex's Batter of the Year.“When I joined Essex, I felt the pressure of having to replace Sir Alastair, but I knew that I needed to bring my own style of cricket,” Elgar said.“I've always had pride in my performances and, naturally, I play this game to win,” he added.Elgar is set to remain available for Essex's final five County Championship matches of the season, beginning with their home fixture against Surrey at Chelmsford.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England v Pakistan: Joe Root shows himself to be the leader England need
articles.summary: Joe Root has shown himself to be the off-field leader England need - now comes a chance to show his credentials as captain on-field.
articles.body:
At the back of the Compton Stand at Lord's is an enormous picture of Ben Stokes.

In the snap, Stokes unleashes a bouncer to a flinching Mohammed Siraj, the India tailender. It was taken during England's heart-stopping 22-run win on this ground last summer.

England's defeat of India was all about Stokes. He made contributions with the bat in both innings, ran out Rishabh Pant with a direct hit and put in a trademark marathon bowling spell on the final day. Stokes came to the post-match media conference with blood seeping through his sock.

Throughout Stokes' tenure as England captain, the question loomed of how anyone would eventually go about succeeding him.

For better or worse, Stokes became the all-encompassing figure in the team, for his performances on the field and what he said or did off it. It was hard to imagine how anyone could emerge from his shadow without having their leadership compared to the talismanic all-rounder.

England are little more than a week into the post-Stokes era and there is already no doubt about the strength of leadership at the helm. This is Joe Root's team now.

The last thing Root would have wanted at the beginning of his second reign as skipper was the Brydon Carse controversy.

Yet, the Yorkshireman has shown himself to be the captain English cricket needs, yet probably does not deserve.

Root's measured, assured and honest address to the media at Lord's on Tuesday was the most impressive display of leadership from anyone connected with the England team in a long time.

Perhaps Root is helped by the circumstances. If Brendon McCullum was still around, he would have been pushed in front of cameras, but McCullum has gone and his replacement Stephen Fleming is yet to arrive. It leaves Root as unquestionably the man in charge.

Root 'hacked off' and 'disappointed' at Carse incident

Root's message has '100%' landed, says Tongue

In terms of Root's second coming as skipper, the off-field part might be the easy bit. It is on the field where he now has a point to prove.

He said as much last week before the Headingley Test - that the biggest challenge in resuming the captaincy was overcoming the perceptions others have of his leadership.

It is not that Root was an awful captain first time around - far from it. It is just the abiding memory is an awful ending of only one win from 17 matches, a horror run that left Root and his team broken.

Leeds was a dream restart, an innings win over Pakistan wrapped up inside three days.

But the one-sided nature of that victory did not give Root room to show what kind of on-field captain he will be this time around. His best act at Headingley was to win the toss and, after Ollie Robinson took a wicket with the first ball of the match, England were on top.

There have been glimpses of what the New Root could become.

Stokes' preference for naming an England team two days before a Test has gone, at least for now. England are likely to be unchanged at Lord's, though that will not be confirmed until the toss.

Root has removed himself from first slip and now fields at mid-off. It may only be a temporary move, but it puts him closer to his bowlers. On the first morning at Headingley, Root yanked a wayward Jofra Archer from the attack after only two overs. It is hard to imagine he would have done the same to either Stuart Broad or James Anderson.

There was a hint of funkiness in the field, albeit an overhang from Root's first spell as captain. The dismissal of Azan Awais in Pakistan's second innings was the eighth time a seamer under Root has had a catch taken at leg slip - the most of any captain since such data began being collected in 2006.

Asked what the difference was between the captaincy of Stokes and Root, fast bowler Josh Tongue said: "It's very chilled out there." Tongue probably did not mean to imply Root brings a greater calmness than Stokes, yet few would argue he has taken the intensity down a notch or two.

For all the impressive media conferences, bowling changes and leg slips, Root will be judged on results, and a win this week would give England their first series triumph since 2024.

There will be plenty of attention on the Lord's pitch, so heavily criticised after England's win against New Zealand. On Wednesday, Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) chairman Mark Nicholas and director of cricket Rob Lynch were seen taking a good look at the surface.

Pakistan should be better than their showing at Headingley, mainly because they cannot get much worse. They are boosted by the return of captain Babar Azam from a hand injury and have won the previous two Tests they have played here.

England will want to build on the green shoots of recovery that sprouted in Leeds.

Jordan Cox impressed at number three and is highly rated by the management. There could be a logjam in the top order when Jacob Bethell returns to fitness, so all of Cox, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence and Jamie Smith will want to ensure they are not squeezed out.

Root said his quartet of fast bowlers "do not know how good they can be". That foursome now have the opportunity to show they can be England's first-choice attack in a range of conditions. It is a bad time for Carse to put himself out of the picture.

As for Root, no man has more runs or hundreds on this ground. Now he returns as the captain, already leading by example this week.

"When you have the privilege of being a leader within a team, you want to build something bigger than just winning," he said. "I feel like I didn't do that very well first time around.

"There's a lot to look forward to, there's a lot to work hard towards. I guess that's the fun side of it."

For Root and his players, following the past few days, the fun side will simply be returning to playing cricket.

articles.title: Brydon Carse: Police investigating alleged assault in connection with nightclub incident involving England bowler
articles.summary: Derbyshire Police said on Wednesday it was investigating allegations of an assault in the city centre, but no arrests have yet been made
articles.body:
Carse was removed from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which begins at Lord's on Thursday morning, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an episode that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a late bar in Derby - then de-arrested after agreeing to depart.

In an updated statement issued on Wednesday evening, Derbyshire Police said: "We are investigating allegations of assault in Derby city centre. No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing."

Further details are unknown, with no clarity over what part - if any - Carse had in the alleged assault.

The England and Wales Cricket Board declined to comment when contacted by the Press Association .

An initial statement from the force, released after a video clip of Carse apparently being detained by officers in the street, had said: "A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."

Former England captain Ben Stokes and centrally contracted seamer Matthew Potts both appeared in the footage, captured in the aftermath of their Durham's side's County Championship victory over Derbyshire, though there is no suggestion that either was involved in anything untoward.

Reacting to the incident, Stokes' replacement as Test skipper Joe Root spoke angrily about the latest in a growing line of alcohol-related issues which have swamped the team.

Root, who made a point of abolishing the midnight curfew which played a partial role in Stokes' exit following another controversial night out earlier this summer, said: "If I'm being brutally honest I'm really hacked off.

"I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person. I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

"But it's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we are doing on the field."
